chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from al-Sindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to me as a visitor, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the profound spiritual merit of *ziyarah* by linking physical visitation to the Prophet with the ultimate eschatological reward of his personal intercession (*shafa'ah*). It reflects the Shia emphasis on the enduring connection between the believer and the Prophet’s legacy, where visiting his grave serves as a tangible means of securing divine favor on the Day of Judgment.
